results.summary: Static security review found no injection, hardcoded secret, SSRF, Struts legacy, or unsafe deserialization markers in the target code. The main gaps are missing Spring Security baseline controls, missing rate limiting/request limits, and incomplete explicit error hardening.

findings.title: No Spring Security baseline, default-deny policy, CSRF configuration, or security headers
findings.description: The application exposes web endpoints without Spring Security in the dependency set and no SecurityFilterChain is present. Even if /api/health and /api/greetings are intentionally public, the code lacks an explicit allowlist/default-deny posture and does not configure standard security headers such as CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. CSRF/session hardening is also absent because Spring Security is not enabled.
findings.evidence: pom.xml declares validation, web, and test starters only. Repository search found no spring-boot-starter-security, SecurityFilterChain, csrf, contentSecurityPolicy, frameOptions, or httpStrictTransportSecurity configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and define a SecurityFilterChain that explicitly permits intended public endpoints, applies anyRequest().authenticated() as fallback, enables CSRF where browser state-changing flows exist, and configures security headers. If this API is intentionally fully public, document that decision and still configure headers.

findings.category: D - Denial of Service / Rate Limiting
findings.title: Public endpoints lack rate limiting and request resource limits
findings.description: The public GET and POST endpoints have validation on the logical name field, but the application does not configure rate limiting, request body limits for JSON, connection/keep-alive timeouts, or related Tomcat safeguards. An attacker can flood /api/greetings or send oversized/slow requests before Bean Validation meaningfully protects business input.
findings.evidence: application.yml only sets server.port and spring.application.name. Repository search found no rate limiting filter/library and no server.tomcat, multipart, connection timeout, or request size limit configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add bounded server settings such as connection timeout, keep-alive timeout, max swallow/request size appropriate to the deployment, and implement per-IP or per-principal rate limiting for public endpoints. Keep validation limits on DTO fields as a second layer.

findings.title: Only validation exceptions are sanitized explicitly; generic error hardening is not configured
findings.description: GlobalExceptionHandler sanitizes validation errors, but it does not explicitly handle malformed JSON or unexpected exceptions, and application.yml does not explicitly disable stack traces/messages in error responses. Spring Boot defaults are generally conservative, so this is a hardening gap rather than confirmed leakage, but production security should not rely on implicit defaults.
findings.evidence: Handlers exist for MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException only. application.yml has no server.error.include-stacktrace or server.error.include-message settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit production-safe settings: server.error.include-stacktrace=never and server.error.include-message=never. Add sanitized handlers for HttpMessageNotReadableException and a final fallback Exception handler that returns a generic response while logging only non-sensitive operational details.

escalations.description: Confirm whether /api/health and /api/greetings are intentionally public for this sample project. If yes, encode that as explicit permitAll rules and document the rationale; if no, require authentication by default.

# Source Code Review Report: Security Review

## Summary
- **Review Target**: full sample-java-code Spring Boot API
- **Verdict**: ❌ Fail
- **Finding Count**: Critical: 0 / High: 2 / Medium: 1 / Low: 0
- **Method**: Static source review only. No files were modified.

## Phase A: Implementation Compliance Check

| OWASP Area | Result |
|---|---|
| A01 Broken Access Control | ⚠️ No Spring Security/default-deny baseline found. Current endpoints may be intentionally public, but this is not explicit. |
| A02 Cryptographic Failures | ✅ No hardcoded secrets or password hashing code found. |
| A03 Injection | ✅ No SQL/JdbcTemplate/native query/command execution patterns found. |
| A07 XSS | ⚠️ No template XSS sink found, but CSP and nosniff headers are not configured. |
| A08 Mass Assignment | ✅ Request body uses GreetingRequest DTO, not entity binding. |
| A10 SSRF | ✅ No RestTemplate/WebClient/user-input URL fetch found. |

## Security Header Check

| Header | Expected | Actual | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-Content-Type-Options | nosniff | Not configured | ❌ |
| X-Frame-Options | DENY | Not configured | ❌ |
| Content-Security-Policy | default-src 'self' | Not configured | ❌ |
| Strict-Transport-Security | enabled in HTTPS deployment | Not configured | ❌ |
| Referrer-Policy | strict-origin-when-cross-origin | Not configured | ❌ |
| Permissions-Policy | camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() | Not configured | ❌ |

## Phase B: STRIDE Attack Resistance Summary

| STRIDE Category | Assessment | Highest Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Spoofing | No auth/session surface in current code, but no security baseline exists for future endpoints. | High |
| Tampering | Greeting input is validated and no business-critical mutable state exists. | Low |
| Repudiation | No security/audit events exist; current app has no admin/payment actions. | Low |
| Information Disclosure | Validation errors are sanitized, but generic error behavior is not explicitly hardened. | Medium |
| Denial of Service | No rate limiting, request size, or connection timeout hardening found. | High |
| Elevation of Privilege | No roles/admin endpoints exist, but no default-deny/method security baseline exists. | High |

## Business Logic Attack Resistance

No EC checkout, price, inventory, coupon, payment, point, cart, or order flow exists in this sample target. Business-logic attack scenarios are not applicable to the current code.

## Consolidated Findings

| # | Severity | Category | Target | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | High | Security baseline | pom.xml:25 | No Spring Security dependency/configuration, default deny, CSRF, or security headers. |
| 2 | High | DoS | application.yml:1 | No rate limiting, request size, or connection timeout limits. |
| 3 | Medium | Information disclosure | GlobalExceptionHandler.java:24 | Only validation exceptions are explicitly sanitized; generic error hardening is implicit/incomplete. |

## Scorecard

| Evaluation Item | Score |
|---|---:|
| Injection Prevention | 5/5 |
| Authentication/Authorization | 2/5 |
| Secret Management | 5/5 |
| Security Headers | 1/5 |
| CSRF Protection | 2/5 |
| Rate Limiting / DoS Defense | 1/5 |
| Spoofing Attack Resistance | 2/5 |
| Tampering Attack Resistance | 4/5 |
| Information Disclosure Resistance | 3/5 |
| Privilege Escalation Resistance | 3/5 |
| Business Logic Attack Resistance | 4/5 |
| Session Management Security | 1/5 |
| Struts Legacy Pattern Safety | 5/5 |
| **Total Score** | **42/65** |

## Escalation Items

Confirm whether all current endpoints are intentionally public. If they are public, configure explicit permitAll rules plus security headers; if not, add authentication and default-deny authorization.

results.summary: Test quality review failed due to strict naming convention violations, unclear AAA structure, insufficient controller error/boundary coverage, and untested public methods shown in the existing JaCoCo report.

findings.title: All test methods violate should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition naming
findings.description: The review standard requires camelCase test names in the should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition form. Current names describe behavior, but none use the required specification-style pattern.
findings.evidence: Violating methods include greetNormalizesRepeatedWhitespace, greetRejectsBlankName, greetRejectsNullName. Controller tests also violate the same pattern at GreetingControllerTest.java lines 25, 32, 39, 50, and 58.

findings.title: Tests do not clearly separate Arrange, Act, and Assert blocks
findings.description: Most tests combine the action and assertion in one expression, and controller tests start directly with mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(...). The required AAA structure is not visible, and Act is not isolated as a single call/result.
findings.evidence: Example: lines 26-28 perform GET /api/health and assert the response in a single chain. GreetingServiceTest lines 14-15 and 20-22 similarly combine Act and Assert.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit Arrange / Act / Assert sections. For MockMvc tests, assign ResultActions result = mockMvc.perform(...); then assert with result.andExpect(...).

findings.title: Tests do not provide @DisplayName descriptions
findings.description: The review standard expects @DisplayName for human-readable test descriptions. None of the eight test methods use @DisplayName, making reports less readable even if method names are improved.
findings.evidence: The test methods are annotated only with @Test. GreetingServiceTest has the same issue at lines 12, 18, and 25.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @DisplayName annotations such as @DisplayName("Returns greeting when query name is valid") above each test.

findings.title: Public methods remain untested in the JaCoCo report
findings.description: The existing JaCoCo report shows missed public methods, which violates the agent rule that all public methods must be tested.
findings.evidence: target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv reports GlobalExceptionHandler with METHOD_MISSED=1 and LINE_MISSED=1; jacoco.xml shows handleInvalidParameter at line 37 missed. SampleJavaCodeApplication.main at line 18 is also missed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a MockMvc test that triggers HandlerMethodValidationException, for example an over-40-character query parameter. Add a Spring context smoke test for the application bootstrap, or explicitly exclude the bootstrap main class from coverage if that is the project policy.

findings.title: Controller error tests are fewer than happy-path tests and miss key validation boundaries
findings.description: The controller suite has three happy-path tests and two error-path tests. It also does not cover missing name, empty JSON, malformed JSON, exact max length 40, or over max length 40 for the @Size(max = 40) validation path.
findings.evidence: Happy paths: healthReturnsUp, greetByQueryReturnsGreeting, greetByBodyReturnsGreeting. Error paths: greetByQueryRejectsBlankName, greetByBodyRejectsBlankName. Production validation includes @NotBlank and @Size(max = 40) at GreetingController.java lines 46-58 and GreetingRequest.java lines 9-12.
findings.suggestedFix: Add parameterized validation tests for blank, missing, and overlong names for both query and body. Add boundary tests for 40-character names accepted and 41-character names rejected.

findings.title: Repeated invalid-name cases are not modeled as parameterized tests
findings.description: The suite tests blank and null service inputs as separate methods and does not cover additional invalid variants. Parameterized tests would reduce duplication and make boundary coverage explicit.
findings.evidence: greetRejectsBlankName and greetRejectsNullName repeat the same assertion shape without @ParameterizedTest/@NullSource/@ValueSource.
findings.suggestedFix: Use @ParameterizedTest with @NullSource and @ValueSource(strings = {"", " ", "\t"}) for invalid names.

escalations.description: The workspace is read-only, so I did not rerun Maven. Findings use source inspection plus the existing target/surefire-reports and target/site/jacoco reports.
